country.comment: The field experiment was conducted across informal settlements (slums) in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 12, Section 'The Mumbai Context'

effect_estimate.comment: Primary 5-year endline outcome is 'full formalization' (verified BMC piped water connection with meter). Joint effect emerges only in policy-eligible settlements and is concentrated in slums requiring multi-agency No Objection Certificates (NOCs) and during the 2020-2022 pre-election window.
effect_estimate.value: In the full sample at endline (N = 6,652 across 76 slums / 152 clusters), neither bureaucratic assistance (T1) alone (0.02, SE = 0.03, one-sided p = 0.26, control mean = 0.43) nor the T1*T2 interaction with political coordination (0.11, SE = 0.08, two-sided p = 0.19; T1 = -0.04 [SE = 0.06], T2 = -0.08 [SE = 0.06], control mean = 0.33) significantly increased verified municipal water connections. In policy-eligible settlements excluding footpaths, forest, and salt pan lands (N = 5,251 across 48 slums), the T1*T2 interaction was 0.22 (SE = 0.10, two-sided p = 0.04; T1 alone = -0.03 [SE = 0.07], T2 alone = -0.06 [SE = 0.07], control mean = 0.42): when combined with political coordination (T2 = 1), bureaucratic assistance (T1) increased verified municipal water connections by 19 percentage points (p = 0.001, ~45% of control mean) and raised progress on the 0-3 formalization scale by 0.39 points (p = 0.046). At 1-year midline in eligible lands (N = 5,010), T1 alone increased formal application submission by 0.10 (SE = 0.03, p = 0.00, control mean = 0.21) and BMC engineer visits by 0.04 (SE = 0.01, p = 0.00, control mean = 0.06), but not P-form approval (0.01, SE = 0.01, p = 0.27) or connections (-0.02, SE = 0.02, p = 0.88). Exploratory NOC subgroup (N = 3,865): T1 marginal effect given T2 = 1 was 26 percentage points (p = 0.006; T1*T2 = 0.31, SE = 0.13, p = 0.051).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cluster-randomized controlled trial appraised with RoB 2 that experimentally manipulates both bureaucratic assistance (petitioning-stage administrative hurdles) and bottom-up political coordination (infrastructural-stage multi-agency and political bottlenecks), directly measuring intermediate administrative steps and verified water connections.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 15-21, Sections 'Experimental Research Design' & 'Empirical Strategy'; PDF pp. 24-33, Sections 'Experimental Results' & 'Mechanisms'

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines legal/policy land eligibility exclusions (post-2000 slums, 2014 Bombay High Court PIL ruling, 2017 BMC exclusions of footpath, forest, and salt pan lands), administrative petitioning burdens (5-15 household group formation, residency/legal-status documentation, plumber sign-off, online filing, fees, site visits, P-forms/C-forms) addressed via NGO bureaucratic assistance (T1), and infrastructural-stage multi-agency fragmentation (land-authority NOCs), bureaucratic/political discretion, delays, and collective citizen participation/political coordination (T2).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Two-level factorial cluster-randomized controlled trial in which T2 (political coordination) was block-randomized at the slum level (76 slums) and T1 (bureaucratic assistance) was randomized at the slum-cluster level (152 clusters).
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 16, Section 'Empirical Strategy'; PDF pp. 18-21, Subsections 'Sampling and Measurement', 'Randomization', & 'Estimation', Figure 4

sample_size.comment: 28 slums (36 clusters) on legally ineligible footpath, forest, and salt pan lands were excluded to form the pre-registered eligible-lands sample (48 slums). Baseline sample was ~6,860-6,863 respondents (Tables S8-S9; 'close to 7,000 households' on p. 3); endline includes 61.5% recontacted baseline respondents plus 2,444 replacement households (N = 6,682 / 5,281 when including the 1 cluster dropped from T1 randomization, Table S17); midline includes 1,466 replacement respondents. Qualitative fieldwork included 6 NGO worker interviews, 2 BMC engineer interviews, and 1 elected corporator interview.
sample_size.value: 76 slums (153 sampled slum clusters; 152 clusters analyzed in main randomization); 6,652 household respondents at endline in full sample (5,251 in eligible-lands sample) and 6,268 at midline (5,010 in eligible-lands sample); plus 9 semi-structured stakeholder interviews

study_design.comment: Interventions fielded May 2018-March 2019 (T2 staggered 5 months after T1); baseline survey Feb-Apr 2018, midline survey Jun-Aug 2019, endline survey May-Sep 2023; supplemented with NGO progress reports and 9 stakeholder interviews.
study_design.value: Multi-level 2x2 factorial cluster-randomized controlled trial (field experiment) block-randomized at the slum level (T2) and complete-randomized at the slum-cluster level (T1), evaluated via baseline, 1-year midline, and 5-year endline household surveys using weighted least squares regression with randomization-block fixed effects, supplemented by qualitative semi-structured interviews and NGO field reports
